title: The Parts share is rounded to the cent and the Labor row gets the rest
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • {Location-A}'s Shop Supplies Charge is 0%, and nothing else is invoiced at {Location-A} today.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} has one labor line of 1.00 hour at $100.00 ($100.00), one part sold at $200.00 and a whole-invoice discount of $1.00; work order {Work-order-2} for {Customer-A} has one labor line of 1.00 hour at $100.00, one part sold at $100.00 and a whole-invoice discount of $0.01. On both, Labor reads {Sales-rep-A} and Parts reads {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001 and {Work-order-2} is S2-40002.
  • Starting screen: the Work Orders page is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Invoice {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2}.
  2. Open Reports > Sales By Representative, set the date range to today, turn Show Unassigned on and turn the Sales Type column on in the column selector.
  3. Read the Adjustments column on the Labor row and on the Parts row of {Work-order-1}'s invoice.
  4. Read the Adjustments column on the Labor row and on the Parts row of {Work-order-2}'s invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: both invoices are created.
  • Step 2: two rows show for each invoice, a Labor row under {Sales-rep-A} and a Parts row under {Sales-rep-B}.
  • Step 3: Parts ($0.67) (the exact share 200 ÷ 300 × 1.00 = 0.666… rounded to the nearest cent) and Labor ($0.33), the rest; together ($1.00).
  • Step 4: each exact share is half a cent, so the Labor row gets the extra cent: Labor ($0.01) and Parts $0.00; together ($0.01).

Chris Ward answered on 19 Oct 2026 how the shares are rounded (answer 21, quoted below); PRD version 10 replaced the earlier rule "A cent left over by rounding the share goes to the Labor row."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R7: “The Parts row's share is rounded to the nearest cent and the Labor row gets the rest, so the two shares always add up to the whole amount. On an exact half cent the Labor row gets the extra cent. Example: labor $100.00, parts $200.00, whole-invoice discount ($1.00): Parts ($0.67), Labor ($0.33).”
  • S5-R6: “Whole-invoice fees and discounts are shared between the Labor and the Parts rows in proportion to each side's labor or parts dollars after that side's line fees and discounts, measured by size whatever their sign. The adjustment that stops a non-taxable discount from taking the subtotal below zero is a whole-invoice amount and is shared the same way. Example: labor $600.00, parts $400.00, shop supplies $30.00, whole-invoice discount ($50.00). The Labor row gets $30.00 supplies and ($30.00); the Parts row gets ($20.00). Subtotals $600.00 and $380.00 add up to $980.00. Each row shows its share in its Adjustments column.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 21: “21. (a) Parts is rounded to the nearest cent and Labor gets the rest; Labor gets the extra cent only on an exact half cent.”
